reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read Saul's inquiry as outwardly formal but insincere, letting Chronicles say he never truly inquired of the Lord at all.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Chronicler's additions to Samuel-Kings as systematic theological idealizing; Saul's death notice in 1 Chronicles 10:14 is one instance.

quotes.text: The alterations and additions of Chronicles are all traceable to the same fountain-head--the Judaising of the past, in which otherwise the people of that day would have been unable to recognise their ideal.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Chronicler's idealizing revisions of Samuel-Kings.

sides.snippet: When Saul inquired of Yahweh, Yahweh didn't answer him, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.
sides.verseText: When Saul inquired of Yahweh, Yahweh didn't answer him, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

sides.snippet: and didn't inquire of Yahweh: therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom to David the son of Jesse.
sides.verseText: and didn't inquire of Yahweh: therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom to David the son of Jesse.
